title: The Jet-Black Mystery Train
notes: GAP: this case spans episodes 701-704 but only subtitle transcripts for 701 and 704 exist locally (702 and 703 are missing). 701 covers the setup (boarding the Bell-Tree Express, the deduction-quiz prank-card confusion over 'Carriage 7 disappearing', and the discovery of Murobashi's body in a chain-locked room) and 704 opens mid-reveal with Kogoro/Conan walking through the full trick, so the mechanics of the murder (stolen uniform, sabotaged bulb, planted watch, mirrored connecting door, chain-lock tampering) are reconstructed from that reveal dialogue rather than being independently observed step by step across the missing middle episodes -- flagged as a fidelity gap, not fabrication. The origin of the prank 'accomplice' cards that caused the Detective Boys' room-swap confusion in 701 is never clarified in the surviving text and is left unencoded (no node/edge asserts who sent them). Detective-cast regulars (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Sonoko, Ai/Haibara as a witness-only presence, Heiji) and the parallel Black Organization/Vermouth-Bourbon-Sherry subplot that runs through 704 are omitted as unrelated to this train murder's suspect pool, matching the convention already used in the old case file and in ep011. Exception: the two passengers registered as 'Natsue Komino' and 'Hiruka Sumitomo' are kept as persons in their own right (not folded into the omitted detective-cast) because the reveal identifies them as Kaitou Kid and an accomplice in disguise, made them part of the on-train suspect pool investigated for the locked-room mystery, and ties directly into a comparative clue (the pyrophobia inconsistency) used in the deduction. CORRECTIONS vs. old cases/ep701-704 file: the old file was structurally thin (single 'events' nodes, a single generic 'knows' edge to the victim for every suspect, motive marked 'unspecified', and objects that stated the killer's identity almost tautologically via 'implicates' with no supporting mechanism). It correctly identified Andō (s1) as the culprit and the correct 5-person suspect pool, but the actual motive (revenge for Andō's wife's death in a fire Murobashi set 5 years ago to cover up an art theft, confirmed on-screen when Andō recognizes a 'destroyed' painting resurfacing at auction two years later) was entirely missing from the old file and is now recovered from the transcript. The old file's claim that the murder weapon was a 'silenced handgun, staged to look like a suicide weapon' is NOT confirmed anywhere in the surviving 701/704 text (only a gunshot smell and a locked room are shown/discussed) -- kept out of the weapon's attrs rather than asserted as fact, likely because that specific detail lived in the missing 702-703 episodes. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Every Carriage 8 passenger is a fire survivor and visibly pyrophobic during the evacuation panic, except 'Komino', who calmly lights her pipe -- the one person unafraid of fire is the one person not really a fire survivor.

A painting everyone assumed burned with the mansion 5 years ago turned up for sale at auction 2 years ago; tracing its ownership led straight back to Murobashi, proving he looted the house before torching it.

Komino and her maid stepped into the corridor at the exact moment the fishing line was rigged to the mirrored door, but the train was passing through a tunnel right then, so the wire went unnoticed in the dark.

edges.detail: recognized the painting at auction 2 years ago and traced its ownership back to Murobashi
spoke joyfully to Andō about the fire that killed Andō's wife, moments before Andō killed him
